type: 短文评论（现象 + 对策）
limit: at least 150 words but no more than 200 words
prompt:
Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

Some parents in China are overprotective of their children. They plan everything for their children, make all the decisions for them, and do not allow them to explore on their own in case they make mistakes or get hurt.
body: Overprotective parenting is common in many Chinese families. Such parents arrange every detail of their children’s lives, from what to eat and wear to which university and major to choose, and they rarely let their children try anything new for fear that they might make mistakes or get hurt.

Although such behavior comes from love, it often does more harm than good. Children who have never made their own decisions may lack independence and confidence, and they may feel lost when they leave home for college or work. Moreover, mistakes and setbacks are an important part of growing up. By shielding children from every risk, parents deprive them of the chance to learn from failure and become resilient.

To address this issue, parents should first change their mindset and realize that letting go is also a form of love. They can begin by giving children age-appropriate responsibilities, such as doing chores or managing their pocket money, and allowing them to make choices and bear the consequences. Schools and communities can also help by offering parenting courses and organizing activities that encourage children to explore on their own. In this way, children will be better prepared for adult life.

type: 短文评论（现象 + 对策）
limit: at least 150 words but no more than 200 words
prompt:
Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

Nowadays star chasing is prevalent among many teenagers. They take pop stars as their idols, imitating their way of talking, following their style of dressing, and seeking every chance to meet them in person at great expenses.
body: Nowadays, many teenagers are devoted fans of pop stars. They regard pop stars as their idols, copy the way they talk and dress, and some even spend large sums of money to see them in person.

Admiring stars is not harmful in itself. A positive idol who works hard and cares about society can inspire young fans to pursue their own dreams. However, blind idol worship can cause serious problems. Some teenagers spend so much time following celebrities online that their studies suffer. Others waste their parents’ hard-earned money on concert tickets, albums and souvenirs. Worse still, when teenagers imitate stars without judgment, they may lose their own identity and adopt distorted values, such as believing that fame and good looks matter more than effort.

To tackle this problem, parents and teachers should guide teenagers to look beyond a star’s appearance and appreciate qualities such as diligence and kindness. Schools can also introduce students to role models in science, sports and public service. In addition, the entertainment industry should stop encouraging irrational spending among fans. Most importantly, teenagers themselves should learn to think independently and treat stars as a source of inspiration rather than the center of their lives.

type: 短文评论（现象 + 对策）
limit: at least 150 words but no more than 200 words
prompt:
Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.

Young people spend a lot of time on the Internet. However, they are sometimes unable to recognize false information on the Internet, judge the reliability of online information sources, or tell real news stories from fake ones.
body: Young people spend a great deal of time online, yet many of them cannot tell true information from false. They often believe sensational headlines, share unverified posts and fail to judge whether a website or an account is reliable.

This phenomenon is worrying. False information can mislead young people in their daily decisions, from what products to buy to how to deal with health problems. When they forward rumors without checking, they also help spread panic and confusion in society. The problem arises mainly because young people tend to trust whatever appears on their screens, and few of them have received training in evaluating information. In addition, some websites deliberately create eye-catching but false stories for clicks.

Several measures can help solve this problem. First, schools should offer courses on media literacy, teaching students how to check sources, compare reports and recognize the common tricks of fake news. Second, online platforms should monitor content more closely, label unverified content and remove rumors promptly. Third, young people themselves should develop the habit of thinking twice before believing or sharing anything. If everyone does their part, young people can become wise users of the Internet rather than victims of false information.

Gross enrolment ratio in higher education in China (1990-2019)

Source: Ministry of Education

【图表】柱状图 + 折线（高等教育毛入学率）：1990 年 3.4%，1995 年 6.86%，2000 年 11%，2001 年 13.3%，2002 年 15%，2003 年 17%，2004 年 19%，2005 年 21%，2006 年 22%，2007 年 23%，2008 年 23.3%，2009 年 24.2%，2010 年 26.5%，2011 年 26.95%，2012 年 30%，2013 年 34.5%，2014 年 37.5%，2015 年 40.0%，2016 年 42.7%，2017 年 45.7%，2018 年 48.1%，2019 年 51.6%
body: The chart shows that the gross enrollment ratio in higher education in China rose dramatically from 3.4% in 1990 to 51.6% in 2019. After modest growth in the 1990s, the ratio climbed rapidly, reaching 21% in 2005 and 30% in 2012. In 2019, it exceeded 50% for the first time, a historic milestone for Chinese higher education.

These figures reflect China’s remarkable achievements in higher education. In just three decades, a college education has changed from a privilege enjoyed by a small minority to an opportunity available to a large share of young people. Millions of students, including many from rural and low-income families, now have the chance to change their lives through knowledge. At the same time, the expansion of higher education has provided the country with a large pool of skilled professionals, supporting its rapid economic development and technological progress.

Nevertheless, expanding enrollment is only the first step. In the future, more attention should be paid to improving the quality of education and making sure that graduates have the skills society needs. When quantity and quality go hand in hand, higher education will contribute even more to the nation’s development.

Degree of urbanization in China from 1980 to 2019

【图表】折线图（城镇化率）：1980 年 19.39%，1985 年 23.71%，1990 年 26.41%，1995 年 29.04%，2000 年 36.22%，2005 年 42.99%，2010 年 49.95%，2011 年 51.27%，2013 年 53.73%，2015 年 56.1%，2016 年 57.35%，2018 年 59.58%，2019 年 60.6%（2012、2014、2017 年只画点、未标数值）
body: As the graph shows, China’s urbanization rate rose steadily from 19.39% in 1980 to 60.6% in 2019. The increase was especially rapid between 1995 and 2010, when the rate jumped from 29.04% to 49.95%. In 2011, it reached 51.27%, passing the 50% mark, meaning that for the first time more Chinese people lived in urban areas than in rural areas. The rate continued to rise after that, though at a slower pace.

This remarkable progress reflects China’s great achievements in urbanization. Hundreds of millions of people have moved from the countryside to cities, where they enjoy better jobs, education and medical care. Modern infrastructure, such as subways, high-speed railways and new residential areas, has transformed the appearance of cities and greatly improved people’s quality of life. Urbanization has also served as a powerful engine of economic growth, creating a huge domestic market and countless new business opportunities.

Of course, rapid urbanization has also brought challenges, such as traffic congestion and high housing costs. Looking ahead, China should pursue people-centered urbanization, making cities greener and more livable while narrowing the gap between urban and rural areas. Then the achievements of urbanization will truly benefit everyone.
